name: OpenSkillEval
intro: OpenSkillEval 是自动审计开放 skill 生态的 Agent 评测框架。它从数据可视化、海报、演示文稿、报告和网页设计五类真实工件或源材料反向构造任务，经结构化规格、自然语言指令与 verifier 形成 677 个动态案例；同时按采用度筛选 30 个社区 skill，在统一 Harbor/Docker 环境中比较无 skill 与强制使用 skill 的 Agent，并从 ATIF 轨迹和最终工件两条通道评测。
org: Singapore Management University, Fudan University, Joy Future Academy, JD
build_method: 工件驱动案例生成, 社区技能时间快照, 受控无技能/强制使用对照, 统一Agent runner
metric: 任务专用工件质量, Skill增益, 轨迹遵循, Token与时间成本
modality: 文本, 图像, 文档, 代码
task_type: Agent任务, 技能评估, 真实工作流
eval_feature: 技能生态审计, 动态任务, 成本质量分析
scale: 677个case：数据可视化150、海报119、演示文稿82、报告195、网页131；30个skills
task_type_en: Agent task, Skill evaluation, Real-world workflow
build_method_en: Artifact-driven Case Generation, Time-snapshot Community-skill Curation, Controlled No-skill/Force-use Comparison, Unified Agent Runner
eval_feature_en: Skill ecosystem audit, dynamic tasks, cost-quality analysis
intro_en: OpenSkillEval automatically audits the open skill ecosystem for LLM agents. It reverse-constructs tasks from artifacts or source materials for data visualization, poster, presentation, report, and web-design work, then produces 677 dynamic cases through a structured specification, a natural-language instruction, and verifier checks. It curates 30 community skills using adoption signals, compares no-skill with force-use agents in a unified Harbor/Docker environment, and evaluates both ATIF trajectories and final artifacts.
scale_en: 677 cases: 150 data visualization, 119 poster, 82 presentation, 195 report, and 131 web design; 30 skills
metric_en: Task-specific Artifact Quality, Skill Gain, Trajectory Adherence, Token and Time Cost

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; source_stage=site-a12c-openskill-pmmeval. OpenSkillEval was reconstructed from the fixed arXiv:2605.23657v2 PDF, SHA-256 15909b00291f602602b8eaddd41769534a60d591f90c06c49e18154be52b7109; the official ALEX-nlp/OpenSkillEval repository at commit d0e109283eee79216284cdf09ee59bf63239fb13; and the official jhying/OpenSkillEval dataset at revision b48e00fc4094fe01c3ef1ee058f0d18c55714f96. The fixed Git README has SHA-256 d7e7b0ce22f89d1bdd4489aaa59d150df56ab24b01f1c9b03a182dda265423e6 and the fixed Hugging Face README has SHA-256 50f0b85fb2fab29cda9e970376a12f393969800cecaac8cd24ab17c6cc4fa121. Sections 2.1–2.3 define two coupled construction tracks rather than one undifferentiated pipeline. The case track first fixes five application families: data visualization, poster generation, presentation generation, report generation, and front-end web design. Category-specific evidence includes open-data portals and academic visualization examples, data-report and promotional poster materials, webpages and documents for slides, awarded or SaaS websites, and real tabular datasets for analytical reports. Each source is snapshot-preserved as a grounded package; the task-generation model then follows a family-specific schema and reverse-constructs a structured task specification T and a natural-language instruction I. The paper names Claude 4.6 Opus and GPT-5.2 as the primary generators. The executable record stores task_input.json, instruction.md, source_brief.md where applicable, and category-specific supporting data such as data.csv or source_data.json. A verifier LLM checks completeness, source grounding, T–I consistency, and compatibility, filtering underspecified, inconsistent, or weakly supported cases. The fixed dataset release and its datasets-server metadata agree on 677 total rows: 150 data-visualization, 119 poster-generation, 82 ppt-generation, 195 report-generation, and 131 web-design. The skill track gathers community skill packs from clawhub.ai, skills.sh, openskills.space, and skillsmp.com, uses adoption and download signals with cost-conscious filtering, and retains 30 skills. The paper and fixed card distribute them as 6 data-visualization, 4 poster, 6 presentation, 6 report, and 8 web skills. Because these marketplaces change, the diagram treats the curated collection as a time snapshot rather than a permanent census. The experiment holds the case, model, and judge fixed while varying a no-skill baseline against force-use skill variants. Appendix A.1 fixes Harbor as the unified execution framework, an ubuntu:24.04 Docker environment, runtime network access, build_timeout_sec=1800.0*5 or 9000 seconds, and timeout_sec=900.0*5 or 4500 seconds. Agents use providers' official Responses APIs and otherwise default agent settings, with installed CLI versions fixed in the authors' environment. Expected artifacts are .pptx for presentations, index.html websites for web design, .png for posters, .html for reports, and .png for data visualization; the runner also captures trajectories, token usage, and wall-clock time. Section 2.3 evaluates behavior and outcome separately. The trajectory branch normalizes traces with ATIF and uses an agent-as-judge to expand the skill into workflow steps, then identifies whether the agent read, followed, skipped, or contradicted those steps. The artifact branch applies family-specific evaluation: presentation rasterization and VLM rubrics; vision- and DOM-grounded browsing plus Playwright navigation, interaction, and data-display checks for web; direct VLM review for poster and data-visualization images; and code-based claim/data checks for reports and data visualization. Pass-rate metrics are linearly mapped to the common 1–5 scale as 4x+1 before aggregation. Appendix A.4 reports human validation on 100 cases balanced across five families by four senior NLP researchers: generated-case quality exceeds 2.98/3 with 98.8% exact agreement. For automatic-judgment quality, the pooled human mean is 2.86/3, four-way exact agreement is 75.0%, and 6.01% of ratings are 1. A separate 200-case Gemini 3.1 Pro robustness check correlates with the primary Claude Opus 4.6 evaluator at Pearson 0.855 and Spearman 0.821. Release boundaries are explicit. The fixed Git repository is Apache-2.0 and contains the runner, agent adapters, entry lists, and per-family evaluator packages; the fixed benchmark cases are CC-BY-NC-4.0. The audited Git tree does not contain the paper's case-generator or case-verifier implementation, but it does contain 30 non-no-skills variant directories under tasks/*/variants/* and 35 tracked environment/skills/**/SKILL.md files at the fixed commit. The curated runner variants are therefore vendored; the unpublished case-generator and case-verifier code remains the release boundary. The official scripts/download_cases.py, SHA-256 dbf192fd90a641e987d2d359e3a2c7437fd5fdf968de6e30abf8785b40bac0f6, calls snapshot_download for jhying/OpenSkillEval but does not pass a revision argument; an ordinary run therefore follows the dataset's moving default branch. The Git and Hugging Face hashes above are audit pins, not values enforced by that helper. Reproduction also depends on Docker, model-provider credentials, external Responses APIs, and the fixed CLI/container environment described but not completely materialized by the public repositories. No formal Draw.io, SVG, PNG, architecture sidecar, catalog, or manifest was changed in this source-stage pass. Formal publication evidence [site-a12c-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2303×1385 (English) and 2306×1385 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2301×1383 and 2304×1383. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
